quote.text:
$ETH Pretty interesting to see how this has moved so far relative to the 2025 move.

- Bottom of this trend started around $1.5K
- Took off with a quick +30% move after retaking $1750
- Rejected $2.8K high timeframe level
- Retested $2.1K high timeframe level

Let's see how we do from here. I've been mentioning these $2.1K and $2.8K levels for the past few years as they have been so influential on Ethereum's price action.

As long as these levels are being respected as strong support & resistances, I would recommend having them on your charts.

I consider this a strong support until it actually breaks lower. For now it can be a good area for a potential higher low to be created.

Most of the 2017 class went broke or quit, brother.

tweets.text:
“We’ve never been hacked” is going to become a much weaker argument for trusting a crypto company.

AI can already help find vulnerabilities that went unnoticed before. It won’t make every system easy to exploit, but it can make finding and testing weaknesses faster.

That should worry any exchange or company that has been getting away with bare-minimum security.

An old audit and a clean track record aren’t enough. Code changes, employee devices get compromised, permissions pile up. Security has to be tested continuously, including how much damage one compromised account can do.

Defenders have access to AI too. Use it to find the gaps, fix them and tighten access before someone else does.

If you custody user funds, your security budget needs to reflect what an attacker can do today.

“We were safe until yesterday” won’t mean much to someone whose savings are gone.
